name: miara (Zig PTHash with PHOBIC bucket assignment, SPIDER-style rank/select, Elias-Fano)
workload: Minimal perfect hash lookups and construction with Elias-Fano encoded pilots, 1M and 100M keys, lambda 6.5 and 3, alpha 0.97, skew and optimal bucket assignment, ten million queries per run.
claimed_speedup: Mixed. Query at 100M keys, lambda 6.5, skew: 45 ns/key (miara) vs 62 ns/key (C++ PTHash); lambda 3: 60 vs 62 ns/key; 1M keys: 35 vs 31 ns/key (miara slower). Optimal bucket assignment: C++ PTHash build at 10M keys did not finish in 20 minutes and its 100M run segfaulted, while miara built 100M keys in 2156 ns/key. The README itself says about 2x slower build than C++ PHOBIC in the main configurations (1779 vs about 1500 ns/key at 100M, 308 vs 120 ns/key at lambda 3).
hardware: Apple M1 series chip (exact model not stated)
tradeoffs: Zig 0.16.0 only; not directly callable from C++ without a C ABI wrapper. Rank/select structures use about 3.1% (rank only) to 11.4% (fast select1) extra space; Select1R 43.71 ns/op and RankDefault 8.18 ns/op on a 100M-value (762.94 MB) bit array at 50% density.
caveats: Single-author, first-party benchmark on one laptop chip with no compiler flags for the Zig build and a C++ baseline built by the author (CMake build took 10 minutes, optimal-BAF runs aborted). Speed claim is mixed and the README admits slower construction. The README gives no numbers against sdsl-lite or sux for its rank/select structures, so no succinct-structure baseline is beaten; entry is the PTHash comparison only. Category fit is marginal (perfect hashing built on Elias-Fano). Found from the GitHub rank-select topic page after HN searches yielded no project with its own benchmark.
